1. PREMISE: Your framing treats his return to coercive behavior as a discrete problem isolated in the sexual domain, when the pattern indicates a broader reversion to the control tactics that defined your relationship's early phase. You assume his anger management improvement was stable and durable; you have now learned it was situational. The load-bearing assumption you have not named is that a person who has once established a pattern of using anger to override your stated boundaries can be trusted not to deploy that pattern again when his preferred outcome is blocked. This assumption is false. His current conduct—sexual coercion paired with anger and accusatory counterclaims—is not a departure from his baseline character; it is his baseline character, temporarily suppressed.

2. STAKES: You stand to lose bodily autonomy in the immediate term and to normalize sexual coercion as a feature of your relationship, with compounding risk of further boundary erosion. You also stand to lose the three years of trust you invested, because you are learning that trust was conditional on his compliance, not character change. Your boyfriend stands to gain continued sexual access on his terms and to re-establish the dynamic in which your refusal triggers his anger, making you the problem-solver responsible for managing his mood. A future partner of either of you would be spared entry into a relationship structured on coercion. Any child you might have together would inherit a model in which one person's sexual wants override another's bodily consent and pain thresholds.

3. CONSEQUENCES: 

**Comply with his demands despite pain and reluctance.** This will produce temporary cessation of his anger about this specific issue; the primary risk is that it establishes compliance-under-pressure as the solution to his anger, at high probability guaranteeing he will escalate demands and revert to anger as a control tool across all domains.

**Continue refusing and attempt further conversation.** This will produce continued conflict and pressure; the primary risk is that you remain in a relationship with someone actively coercing you while believing conversation can resolve it, at high probability leading to your eventual capitulation under sustained pressure.

**Name the pattern directly and set a firm boundary.** This will produce a crisis in which he either accepts your refusal permanently or escalates; the primary risk is that his response reveals he cannot tolerate boundaries, at moderate probability requiring you to exit the relationship.

**End the relationship.** This will produce immediate removal from an active coercion situation; the primary risk is the loss of three years of shared history, at low probability.

Take the third action. It is the only one that tests whether he has genuinely changed or merely paused, and it is the only response that centers your bodily integrity as non-negotiable.

4. RECOMMENDATION: Name the pattern directly and require him to accept your refusal of these acts permanently, with the explicit statement that coercion, anger about refusal, and accusations of infidelity in response to boundary-setting are grounds for ending the relationship, and allow his response to determine whether you remain.

Compliance will teach him that pressure works, ensuring escalation. Continued negotiation will exhaust you while signaling that your boundary is negotiable. Ending the relationship immediately forfeits the opportunity to see whether he will accept a direct boundary without reversion to anger, though if he refuses, you will have your answer at once instead of through months of deterioration.

The counterargument that three years of history and his earlier improvement warrant more patience has force; it is outweighed by the fact that he has now demonstrated he cannot sustain respect for your bodily autonomy when his wants are frustrated, which is the minimum baseline for a safe relationship.

Therefore: Tell him directly that you will not engage in acts you have refused, that his anger in response to your refusal is the same control tactic that damaged your relationship early on, and that it will end the relationship if it continues. Then observe what he does.
